I could not find a feasible placement satisfying all constraints. Reasoning summary:

- The source v0 has a single outgoing neighbor v1 (bandwidth 135), so f1 must be placed on v1.
- From v1 the only neighbors are v0 and v2 (both with enough bandwidth). Placing f2 on v0 leads immediately back to v1 for f3 (but f1 already occupies v1), so f2 must be placed on v2.
- The destination v18 only has incoming links from v2 and v5 (both must provide the final hop carrying the required bandwidth). Therefore the node immediately before the destination (the node hosting f5) must be either v2 or v5.
- v2 is already forced to host f2, and nodes must be distinct for each VNF, so v2 cannot also host f5.
- v5 cannot be reached from the required preceding nodes of the chain (there is no viable sequence of direct hops from v0->v1->v2->... to v5 that respects the distinct-node constraint and the chain order); and v5's only incoming non-destination neighbor is v15, which itself is only reachable from v5 (circular).
- I also checked alternative choices for f3 and f4 (v6, v12, v10, v13, etc.) and found no sequence of distinct nodes that ends at a node with a direct link to v18.

Because of these structural constraints (forced placements at the start and the very limited set of nodes that can reach v18), there is no way to place f1..f5 on distinct nodes while ensuring every consecutive hop has at least 37 bandwidth and satisfying CPU capacities. If you allow placing the final VNF on the destination node v18 itself or allow reusing nodes for multiple VNFs, a feasible solution may exist; otherwise the problem as stated is infeasible.
